title: Ragusan maritime quarantine
summary: Ragusa imposed a thirty-day waiting period on arrivals from plague-affected places before they entered the city.

title: Chadwick's sanitary report
summary: A systematic survey documented how urban housing, waste, and water conditions contributed to illness and premature mortality.

title: Liverpool Medical Officer of Health
wiki: History of public health in the United Kingdom
summary: Liverpool appointed William Henry Duncan as the first Medical Officer of Health in the United Kingdom to address municipal sanitation and population health.

title: Public Health Act 1848
wiki: History of public health in the United Kingdom
summary: The Act established a General Board of Health and authorized local boards and medical officers to manage sanitation and health conditions.

parents.reason: Chadwick's investigation documented sanitation conditions and helped prompt government inquiry and legislation.

title: Slow sand filtration
summary: John Gibb installed Robert Thom’s experimental sand filter at a Paisley bleachery in 1804 and sold surplus filtered water to the public; later refinements supplied Chelsea Waterworks in 1829.

title: Metropolis Water Act 1852
summary: London law regulated water sources and required water companies to filter domestic supplies before distribution.

parents.reason: Existing sand-filter installations supplied a practical treatment method for the Act's filtration requirement.

title: London Main Drainage
summary: Bazalgette's interceptor and street sewers diverted London's raw sewage away from streets and the tidal Thames.

parents.reason: Covered sewer conduits supplied the physical collection and conveyance method expanded into London's interceptor network.

title: New York City Metropolitan Board of Health
wiki: History of public health in the United States
summary: A citywide health board used inspections, sanitation rules, disinfection, and quarantine to manage disease outbreaks and environmental hazards.

title: Continuous municipal water chlorination
summary: Continuing chlorine doses disinfected municipal drinking-water supplies and stopped waterborne outbreaks.

parents.reason: Recognition that microbes cause disease supplied the rationale for disinfecting water against microbial contamination.

title: Activated sludge wastewater treatment
summary: Aeration and recycled microbial floc biologically removed organic pollution from sewage at treatment works.

parents.reason: Sewer networks collected the wastewater that the aerated biological process treated at a sewage works.

title: Community water fluoridation
summary: Public water systems adjusted fluoride concentrations to reduce tooth decay across a community.

parents.reason: Municipal water-distribution pipes carried a measured additive to households across the service area.

title: International Sanitary Conferences
summary: A series of government meetings sought shared rules for quarantine and responses to cholera, plague, and yellow fever across borders.

title: Pan-American Sanitary Bureau
summary: Governments of the Americas established a continuing regional organization for public-health cooperation and disease control.

parents.reason: WHO’s history links the bureau’s 1902 founding in part to the earlier sanitary-conference series.

title: International Classification of Diseases
summary: The Bertillon cause-of-death scheme began a standardized classification later revised for comparable morbidity and mortality statistics.

parents.reason: Official death records supplied events that the classification grouped into comparable cause-of-death categories.

title: Centralized U.S. Marine Hospital Service
summary: A federal reorganization placed previously local marine hospitals under a centrally managed bureau and supervising surgeon.

title: U.S. National Quarantine Act and epidemic reporting
summary: Federal law assigned quarantine authority to the Marine Hospital Service and required consulates to send weekly reports of epidemic infections.

parents.reason: The Act vested federal quarantine and epidemic-reporting duties in the centrally administered Marine Hospital Service.

title: United States Public Health Service
summary: The Marine Hospital Service took the Public Health Service name as its federal responsibilities expanded to quarantine, disease control, health statistics, and research.

parents.reason: The Public Health Service was the renamed and expanded continuation of the Marine Hospital Service.

title: U.S. Public Health Reports
summary: A federal publication printed weekly reports of epidemic infections required under U.S. quarantine law.

parents.reason: The reporting duties created by the Quarantine Act supplied the weekly epidemic reports published by the Surgeon General.

title: Office of Malaria Control in War Areas
wiki: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
summary: A wartime U.S. program used mosquito abatement and habitat control to reduce malaria around military and defense-production areas.

parents.reason: The Public Health Service's malaria-control program and personnel formed the agency that later became CDC.
Knowing that mosquitoes carry malaria gave the program a target for abatement and habitat-control work.

title: Communicable Disease Center
wiki: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
summary: The Communicable Disease Center began in Atlanta as the successor to wartime malaria-control work, with mosquito abatement as its primary activity.

parents.reason: The center was founded as the successor to the wartime malaria-control program.
The new center began as a branch of the U.S. Public Health Service.
parents.directContribution: The Center began as an operating branch of the Public Health Service; this direct administrative placement is distinct from inheriting the malaria-control program through its predecessor.

title: Weekly Morbidity Report
summary: A federal weekly publication moved morbidity and mortality statistics into a dedicated report for public-health monitoring and recommendations.

parents.reason: Morbidity and mortality statistics were transferred from Public Health Reports into the new weekly publication.

title: World Health Organization
summary: A UN specialized agency inherited international disease-coordination and public-hygiene functions from earlier health organizations.

parents.reason: The United Nations established WHO as a specialized agency for international health coordination.
WHO incorporated the Paris office’s staff, assets, and duties into the new international health agency.
WHO incorporated the League health organization’s staff, assets, and public-health duties.

title: International Health Regulations 1969
summary: WHO rules required states to notify the organization about specified international disease threats, including cholera, yellow fever, and plague.

parents.reason: WHO provided the international authority and channel through which member states reported specified disease events.

title: Public health nursing
summary: Lillian Wald established Henry Street Settlement in 1893 and coined public-health nursing for neighborhood service addressing family and community health needs.

title: New York City school medical inspection
summary: New York City began municipal medical inspections of pupils at school, identifying health conditions that could affect children and their learning.

parents.reason: Public schools brought large groups of children into an organized setting where health inspections could reach them.

title: Office International d’Hygiène Publique
summary: An international public-hygiene office was established in Paris after the sanitary conferences; WHO later incorporated its staff, assets, and duties.

parents.reason: WHO’s history attributes the office’s establishment in part to the achievements of the international sanitary conferences.

title: Health Organization of the League of Nations
wiki: Health Organization of the League of Nations
summary: The League established a dedicated health organization in 1920; WHO later incorporated its staff, assets, and public-health duties.

parents.reason: The League established this health organization as a dedicated component of its international work.
